notes: The original-side locator and neutral description are empty. Primary article title and author verified. No outcome, predictor, model, or test is supplied for this row; es_type ser_method does not establish a metric or identify a test. Table 1 (printed p. 1661; PDF p. 18) has three FE-GLS models and many unstandardized coefficients: model 1 domestic causes, model 2 global causes, model 3 combined causes. Candidate analytic Ns are model 1 = 566, model 2 = 397, model 3 = 566 country-year observations, across 18 countries (countries are panel units, not observation N). Table 2 (PDF p. 21) models 3–5 and appendix Table A1 (printed p. 1672) report N observations = 566; this is not common to every model in the paper. Methods pp. 1655–1658 describe a maximum of 612 observations, missing trade data for Switzerland and New Zealand in 1991–2003, numerous missing FDI country-years, seven Hadi outliers (Norway 1999–2003; Belgium 1998–99), and one-year lags. No recruitment total or df-derived N is used; no N sum or effect conversion is performed. Candidate coefficient/p pairs include Table 1 model 2 imports South −.828 with *** (P < .001), exports South .192 with *** (P < .001), imports North −.058 with * (P < .05), exports North .062 with * (P < .05), and FDI −.011 with no star (no exact p printed). These are candidates only, not assigned target estimates. Table 1 and Table 2 model 3 national-affluence-cubed star counts differ (** versus ***), so their p bounds must not be merged. Table 3 reports attributable percentages of change, not a uniquely identified row target. All assigned values remain null because correspondence cannot be established. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
